provenance.construction: Cyclic generalized-bicycle code on the ring x^337 - 1 with H_X = [circ(a) | circ(b)] and H_Z = [circ(b)^T | circ(a)^T]. Both a and b lie in the ideal generated by a divisor of x^337 - 1 whose degree fixes k = 2 deg gcd(a, b, x^337 - 1).
provenance.notes: m = 337 is prime with ord_2(m) = 21, so the only proper divisor of m is 1 and every quotient fold is vacuous: the ceiling (m/t) d_t that binds a composite modulus does not exist here. That leaves two mechanisms. The orbit fold over every equal-orbit partition of the qubits returns nothing lighter than the claim. The single-block logicals of H_X form the cyclic code of dimension deg g whose zeros are the residues the divisor leaves out, and the coset subset is chosen among those reachable at the target degree to maximise the longest run of consecutive residues among them, which is what the Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem bound reads; a direct search confined to one circulant block at 12 seeds of 600,000 trials confirms it. The distance is a witness-backed upper bound from a 24-seed gate at 2,000,000 information-set trials per seed.
